To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the artificial A•T hook proteins D1 and Math20 compete for binding in vitro to identical sites on the pericentric satellite III repeats of Drosophilas X chromosome, and that this competition is reflected in vivo by a displacement of the D1 protein from its preferred binding site in the pericentric hetero‐chromatin.

the suppression of position‐effect variagtion (PEV) by MATH20 in Drosophila is due to a competition for binding to the same sites of the pericentric satellite III repeats by MATH20 and the A•T‐Hook protein D1.
the A•T‐Hook protein D1 binds AT‐rich hetero‐chromatin and that the A•C‐Hook protein MATH20 suppress the binding of D1 to heterochromatin and thus suppress the variegation phenotype of wm4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of heterochromatin assembly in Drosophila melanogaster.
the molecular mechanisms of position‐effect‐variegation (PE‐var) in Drosophila and the role of the A•T‐rich satellite III (SAT‐III) repeats of chromosome 1 in this process.
the role of Drosophia A•T‐hooks in the assembly of the AT‐rich pericentric heterchromatin and the consequences of this role for the regulation of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MATH20‐D1 system represents a novel mechanism to control PEV.
the MATH20 protein is able to displace the D1 protein from its preferred binding to AT‐rich satellite III repeats.
D1 is an A•T‐rich satellite III‐specific heterochromatin protein that is required for heterochromatic silencing of the white gene in the wm4 position‐effect varigation (PEV) system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the A•T‐hooks are the first example of a family of sequence‐specific DNA‐binding proteins that are involved in the assembly of pericentric hetero‐ and euchromatin in Drosophila and that they are likely to have a similar role in mammalian heterochromatin.
the competition for binding to SATIII repeats is a mechanism for the modification of PEV by D1 and M3.
D1 binds to SATIII repeats, which in turn recruits a protein partner, possibly the heterochromatin protein HP1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the suppression of position‐effect‐variegation by the A•T‐binding protein MATH20 is mediated by a competitive displacement of the D1 protein from pericentric AT satellite DNA.
competition for binding to the same site of a satellite repeat is a powerful tool for modulating the position‐effect variances in a Drosophila model system.
the suppression of PEV by MATT20 is not due to a direct interaction between MATH20 and the white gene but rather is due to a competition with D1 for binding to SATIII repeats.
